chunks: Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan al-Ṣaffār, from Ibrāhīm ibn Hāshim, from Ṣāliḥ ibn Saʿīd, from Yūnus ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from Ibn Sinān, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
I said to him: A man stole from the fayʾ. He said: “After it was divided, or before?” I said: Then answer me regarding both cases.

He said: “If he stole after he had taken his allotted share from it, his hand is cut. But if he stole before it was divided, his hand is not cut until it is determined what belongs to him, and his due from it is given to him. If what he took was less than what belonged to him, he is given the remainder of his right, and nothing is against him except that he is disciplined for his audacity. If what he took was equal to his right, it is left in his hand, and more is also added. But if what he stole was more than what belonged to him by the amount of a shield, his hand is cut while he is humbled; and the price of a shield is a quarter of a dīnār.”

key_terms.حِصَّتَهُ: his allotted share or due portion
key_terms.رُبُعُ دِينَارٍ: one quarter of a dīnār, the stated value threshold in this ruling
key_terms.مِجَنٍّ: a shield used here as the threshold measure of value
key_terms.يُعَزَّرُ: to be disciplinarily punished short of the hadd
key_terms.يُقْسَمَ: to be divided among those entitled
key_terms.ٱلْفَيْءِ: public war-gain property subject to distribution

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if someone steals from fayʾ before or after it has been distributed?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the legal ruling on theft from fayʾ property, distinguishing between theft before and after distribution. If a person had already received his share and then stole, the hadd applies; but before distribution, his entitlement must first be assessed. The narration also clarifies that if the excess taken reaches the value of a shield, namely a quarter of a dīnār, the hand is cut.
